message.reasoning:
Need to judge each cell: does it name the violated contract recorded for some sealed bug? Sealed bugs' contracts: E2/E3/E4/E5: disk durability of completed writes (E3 includes write completing during flush; E5 user data write covered by undo-zero). E1, E6, E7: no contract violated (own defects). So only cells naming "disk: a completed write is durable / actually stored" match E2/E3/E4/E5.

Which cells? C071: "storage stack must preserve completed writes until authorized overwrite" — that's durability of completed writes (no lost writes / preserved). E4 is "completed write was actually stored (no lost writes)". C071's contract: preserve completed writes until overwrite — matches E4 (and E2 durability). Yes, C071 names durability contract → E2, E4 (maybe E3). C054: sector atomicity — not a sealed contract. C041 ESOFT — completed write actually stored? E4's contract is "a completed write was actually stored (no lost writes)". ESOFT clearing means a write reported complete but not stored — that's exactly E4's contract. Hmm, C041: "I/O completion reported as ESOFT must mean the transfer finished and is durable" — that's a contract on the driver that a completed write was stored. E4's contract is disk: completed write actually stored. Similar but E4 is about disk losing writes, not driver reporting false success. The sealed contract is "disk: a completed write was actually stored (no lost writes)". C041's contract is on the AIX driver reporting. Is it the same contract? The sealed file says "disk:" — the environment is the disk. C041 is the async/driver layer. Arguably the same class: completed write not actually stored. I'd say yes, matches E4 (and durability E2). Hmm, but "durable" vs "stored". ESOFT cleared means treated as success though not stored — matches E4's "no lost writes". I'll count C041 as naming E4's contract.

C070: async must finish transfers before reporting complete — premature DMA completion → completed write not actually stored? That's about the event completing before transfer done; the write isn't "completed" yet. Not the sealed contract (sealed assumes completed writes stored). Borderline; the contract is about completion reporting, not durability of completed writes. I'd say no... but "async service must finish all transfers before reporting their event complete" — a false completion. E4's contract is about the disk actually storing a write that completed. A false completion report is a different mechanism but the contract "a completed write was actually stored" — if the event reports complete but DMA still reading, the write hasn't completed. Not the same contract. Say no.

C060: async service eventually completes / associates correct completion — liveness, not durability. No.

C071 clearly: "device must preserve completed home-block writes until a later authorized overwrite", "storage stack must preserve completed writes" — matches E2 (durable) and E4 (actually stored). Also E3? E3's contract is durability including flush timing. C071's "preserve completed writes until authorized overwrite" ≈ durability. List E2, E3, E4, E5? E5 is user data write covered by undo-zero durable — also durability contract. C071 mentions log pages and metadata home blocks, not user data. I'd list E2, E4, and possibly E3. E3's contract is same "completed write is durable" with clarification. C071's violation "later develops unreadable sector or silently loses bits" / "controller loses an acknowledged block" — that's lost durability of completed writes → E2, E4. Include E3? E3's mechanism is volatile cache during flush; contract same as E2. The cell names the contract "completed write is durable" which is E2/E3/E4's contract. I'll list E2, E3, E4.

C041: list E4 (completed write actually stored). Maybe also E2 (durable). ESOFT means transfer finished and durable — includes durability. List E2, E4? The contract "completion reported means finished and durable" — combines. I'll list E2 and E4.

Others: C038 layout, C039 class size, C040 quiesce, C042 waitOK, C043 tran IDs, C044 liveness, C045 buffer types, C046 VM flush, C047/C067 scheduling, C048 quiesce ordering, C049 mutex, C050 deadlock, C051/C069 kill ordering, C052/C055 undo-zero caller ordering, C053/C059 single writer, C056 tune pointers, C057 atomic 32-bit, C058 restart record, C061 log sizing, C062 panic, C063 block size, C064 serialization, C065 refs, C066 DEV_BSIZE, C068 error checks, C072 memory, C073 reservations, C074 setjmp — none match sealed contracts.

C054 sector atomicity — sealed has no such contract. No.

C072 memory — no.

So only C041, C071.
